title: Gradients: the direction of steepest increase

steps.label: The loss landscape from above
steps.pseudocode: The loss of two weights is a landscape. Its lowest point is the best setting.

steps.label: Where the model is now
steps.pseudocode: The model currently has weights (1, 3). Compute the loss there.

steps.label: The slope along w1
steps.pseudocode: Partial derivative of the loss with respect to w1.

steps.label: The slope along w2
steps.pseudocode: Partial derivative of the loss with respect to w2.

steps.label: Combine them into the gradient
steps.pseudocode: gradient = [partial for w1, partial for w2]

steps.label: The gradient points steepest uphill
steps.pseudocode: The length of the gradient says how steep the climb is.

steps.label: Flip it to go downhill
steps.pseudocode: The downhill direction is the negative gradient: flip the sign of every entry.
steps.python:
g = [-4, 8]
downhill = [-v for v in g]
print(downhill)   # [4, -8]

steps.label: Repeat from the new point
steps.pseudocode: Step a little against the gradient, recompute the gradient there, and repeat.
